A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Robust Sample-based PMD-PD and MDPO-Robust-Lag work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices E–G report original training, robustness-test, and schedule-comparison results on Cartpole and two inventory-management domains.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendices F–H report original experiments on the same three domains, with revised benchmark results and expanded schedule comparisons.

M1.justification: V2 introduces Approximate TMA with sampled action-next-state values and tabular or function-approximation branches (Algorithm 1). Algorithms 2–3 invoke this subroutine in place of v1's generic LTMA loop, materially extending the proposed transition optimizer. Appendix E clarifies that the experiments still use Monte Carlo TMA.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Cartpole, scalar Inventory Management, and 3-D Inventory Management with the same constraints, dynamics families, uncertainty sets, and distortion-test scenarios. The expanded schedule experiments remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2–4 retain the MCPMD, PPO, and MDPO families and their robust/constrained variants. Within the schedule comparison, however, v2 adds unconstrained MDPO-Robust; v1's Appendix G compared only MDPO-Robust-Lag and MDPO-Robust-Augmented-Lag.

E3.justification: The main robust-constrained MDPO experiments switch from restart scheduling in v1 to fixed alpha = 2 in v2. Additional schedule protocols distinguish epoch-based and batch-based updates, with geometric schedules initialized at 5 and 2 respectively. Domain hyperparameters, training budgets, test grids, and main evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1's Appendix G compares linear, restart, and geometric schedules. V2's Appendix H substantially expands this sensitivity study with a fixed schedule, separate epoch-based and batch-based scheduling, and unconstrained MDPO-Robust. It therefore tests update frequency as well as schedule form, while retaining and revising the existing training and distortion analyses.

E5.justification: The stated ten-seed evaluations and uncertainty-estimation practices remain unchanged: training plots report standard errors across seeds, while test tables report standard errors across environments. Expanded schedule tables continue using means, standard errors, and minima without introducing a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 extensively revise MDPO scores and some rankings. For example, Table 4b reports MDPO-Robust-Augmented-Lag's mean positive penalised return as -928.3 with v1's restart setting and -1219.2 with v2's fixed setting; these are different configurations. PPO-Robust's mean return also changes from 60.7 to 60.9. Tables 11–12 add many schedule-result entries.

T1.justification: V2 removes v1's oracle policy-convergence theorems in Section 4.3 and their supporting Appendix B, adds Approximate TMA regret and sample-complexity proofs, and substantially rewrites the main sample-complexity argument. It adds a bounded-dual-variable assumption and strengthens Slater's condition from kernel-specific feasible policies to one policy feasible for every kernel. New transition-change, Bregman, and dual-error bounds appear in Appendix D.6.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion withdraw v1's O(1/T) and exponential oracle policy-convergence claims. V2 instead presents Approximate TMA as an independent contribution and supports the retained sample-based convergence claim with explicitly sampled transition updates.

C2.justification: V1 describes its Lagrangian formulation as equivalent to the constrained objective; v2 distinguishes the conventional RCMDP objective from the related single-simulator robust Lagrangian. V2 also discusses why Slater points need not guarantee RCMDP strong duality, explains additional applicability assumptions, and revises schedule recommendations toward a fixed default with problem-dependent benefits from varying schedules.

D1.justification: V2 supplies schedule initialization values, discloses joint critic/policy updates, and clarifies that the empirical LTMA implementation uses Monte Carlo rather than the proposed additional function approximation. These are added documentation details; the architecture and hyperparameter Tables 8–10, hardware description, and code-source access information are retained.

R1.justification: A dedicated related-work section substantially expands positioning around robust objectives, adversarial kernels, uncertainty-set construction, and policy optimization. Added works include Behzadian et al., Germano et al., Grand-Clément et al., and Wiesemann et al. The change from Wang and Petrik (2024) to Wang et al. (2024) identifies the same titled work and is not counted as a new work.

P1.justification: The introduction and theoretical narrative are substantially rewritten and reorganized. V2 adds a dedicated related-work section, moves the principal algorithm pseudocode to Appendix B and the full sample-complexity proof to Appendix D, and relocates the restart discussion to Appendix H.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned from two related-work overviews into a unified comparison with explicit parameterization and convergence-rate columns. The schedule display expands into two tables with additional return columns and domain blocks. Main figures and tables are resized or relocated, and several retained plots have revised axis ranges.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful schedule controls, clarifies assumptions, and attempts to close v1's explicit oracle-LTMA gap with a sampled transition optimizer. However, its new Lemma 26 applies a multiplicative value bound to permitted signed costs; this bound fails even for identical kernels with a negative constant cost. Because that lemma supports the revised central guarantee, the added analysis does not reliably establish that the theoretical gap is resolved. The net quality effect therefore remains uncertain.
